newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus renews call for dialogue with NATO.
newsitem.headline: Belarus renews call for dialogue with NATO.

text.p: Belarus on Tuesday renewed its call for political dialogue with NATO but repeated its opposition to the Western defence alliance's planned expansion eastward.

Belarussian Foreign Minister Ivan Antonovich told diplomats in Minsk on Tuesday that Belarus wanted to participate in NATO's Partnership for Peace programme after years of boycotting it despite formal membership.
"The Republic of Belarus still thinks NATO expansion is a mistake," said a foreign ministry statement faxed to Reuters. But "constructive political dialogue with NATO has been proposed."
"This productive dialogue between Minsk and Brussels could significantly strengthen security in the region," it added.
Belarus shares neighbouring Russia's opposition to plans by NATO to expand eastwards, but welcomed last week's deal on forming a new partnership between Moscow and the Western alliance.
"Belarus intends to take part in the Partnership for Peace," the statement said.
"The Belarussian side already has completed the individual programme of partnership with NATO and would send it to the NATO headquarters as a basis for its participation in PFP."

Hardline President Alexander Lukashenko, who once described NATO as a "dreadful monster", called earlier this year for the conclusion of the treaty between his country and NATO. Lukashenko also said a new "European order" should be established without the United States.
